attractions.name: Petronas Towers
attractions.desc: Once the tallest buildings in the world, these twin towers remain Kuala Lumpur's defining landmark, connected by a skybridge on the 41st and 42nd floors. An observation deck near the top offers wide city views, best booked in advance given limited daily tickets. The surrounding KLCC park and mall make it easy to spend a full afternoon in the area.

attractions.name: Batu Caves
attractions.desc: A limestone hill riddled with cave temples dedicated to the Hindu god Murugan, reached by climbing 272 brightly painted steps guarded by a towering golden statue at the base. The main cave functions as an active place of worship, especially during the Thaipusam festival. It's a short trip from central Kuala Lumpur.

attractions.name: George Town, Penang
attractions.desc: A UNESCO-listed old port city known for its mix of Chinese, Malay, Indian, and colonial British architecture within a compact, walkable core. Street art, working clan jetties, and some of the country's best hawker food make it a favorite stop for a slower few days. Its food scene alone draws repeat visitors.

attractions.name: Cameron Highlands
attractions.desc: A cool mountain plateau covered in rolling tea plantations, strawberry farms, and patches of mossy forest, a sharp contrast to the tropical heat elsewhere in the country. Guided jungle walks pass through the Mossy Forest's stunted, lichen-draped trees. Tea estate tours and tastings are the main draw for most visitors.

attractions.name: Kinabalu National Park, Borneo
attractions.desc: Home to Mount Kinabalu, Southeast Asia's tallest peak outside the Himalayas, climbable over two days by most reasonably fit hikers with a permit and guide. The surrounding park also protects extraordinary biodiversity, including carnivorous pitcher plants found nowhere else. It's usually paired with a trip to see orangutans elsewhere in Sabah.

attractions.name: Semenggoh Wildlife Centre
attractions.desc: A rehabilitation center in Sarawak, Borneo, where semi-wild orangutans that were once orphaned or injured return during scheduled feeding times. Sightings aren't guaranteed since the orangutans forage freely in surrounding forest, which adds to the appeal of seeing them in a genuinely wild-adjacent setting. It's one of the more accessible ways to see orangutans in Malaysian Borneo.

itinerary.label: Days 1–3
itinerary.title: Kuala Lumpur
itinerary.desc: The Petronas Towers, Batu Caves, and the city's varied food scene.
itinerary.cost: Petronas Towers Skybridge and observation deck tickets cost about MYR 98; Batu Caves entry is free.
itinerary.food: Try nasi lemak from a street stall for breakfast — genuinely eaten that way by locals.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Cameron Highlands
itinerary.desc: Tea plantations and a cool-climate break from the tropical lowlands.
itinerary.cost: Tea plantation tours cost about MYR 5–15 for basic entry.
itinerary.food: Try a pot of fresh Cameron Highlands tea with scones — a colonial-era holdover that's become a genuine local specialty.

itinerary.label: Days 5–6
itinerary.title: Penang
itinerary.desc: George Town's old streets, street art, and hawker food.
itinerary.cost: Most of George Town's street art and old streets are free; a hawker meal costs MYR 8–15.
itinerary.food: Char kway teow from a well-reviewed hawker stall is the Penang dish to prioritize.

itinerary.label: Days 7–10
itinerary.title: Borneo (Sabah/Sarawak)
itinerary.desc: Orangutan sightings and, for the more ambitious, a climb of Mount Kinabalu.
itinerary.cost: A guided orangutan sanctuary visit costs about MYR 30–50; a river cruise for wildlife spotting runs MYR 150–300.
itinerary.food: Try Sarawak laksa, distinct from the Peninsula versions, if visiting that side of Borneo.

goodToKnow.tipping: Not obligatory; service charge is often already included
goodToKnow.safety: Very safe; normal precautions apply in busy city areas
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Domestic flights are the easiest way to reach Borneo from the peninsula
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KUL) is the main gateway for this route

food.name: Nasi lemak
food.desc: Coconut rice served with sambal, fried anchovies, peanuts, and egg — considered the national dish.

food.name: Char kway teow
food.desc: Stir-fried flat rice noodles with prawns, egg, and bean sprouts, a Penang specialty.

food.name: Laksa
food.desc: A spicy noodle soup with regional variations ranging from curry-based to tangy tamarind broths.

food.name: Roti canai
food.desc: A flaky flatbread served with curry sauce for dipping, popular any time of day.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Malaysia?
faq.a: Not for most Western passport holders for short tourist stays.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Kuala Lumpur International (KUL), the country's main gateway.

faq.q: Do I need to book orangutan viewing in Borneo in advance?
faq.a: Recommended for the better-known sanctuaries and river cruises, especially in peak season, though some centers accept walk-ins.
No, genuinely affordable — one of the better values in Southeast Asia for food, transport, and accommodation.

daysReason: 10 days covers Kuala Lumpur, the Cameron Highlands, Penang, and Borneo without rushing. 5–6 works for just the peninsula; 12–14 lets you slow the Borneo leg down considerably.
visa: Not required for most Western passport holders for short stays — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Torres Petronas
attractions.desc: Outrora os edifícios mais altos do mundo, estas torres gémeas continuam a ser o marco definidor de Kuala Lumpur, ligadas por uma ponte no 41º e 42º andar. Um miradouro perto do topo oferece vistas amplas da cidade, embora seja melhor reservar com antecedência dado o número limitado de bilhetes diários. O parque e centro comercial KLCC circundante tornam fácil passar uma tarde inteira na zona.

attractions.name: Grutas de Batu
attractions.desc: Uma colina calcária cheia de templos em grutas dedicados ao deus hindu Murugan, alcançável subindo 272 degraus pintados de cores vivas guardados por uma imponente estátua dourada na base. A gruta principal funciona como local ativo de culto, especialmente durante o festival Thaipusam. Fica a uma curta distância do centro de Kuala Lumpur.

attractions.name: George Town, Penang
attractions.desc: Uma antiga cidade portuária classificada pela UNESCO, conhecida pela sua mistura de arquitetura chinesa, malaia, indiana e colonial britânica dentro de um centro compacto e caminhável. Arte de rua, cais de clãs em funcionamento, e alguma da melhor comida de rua hawker do país tornam-na uma escolha preferida para uns dias mais lentos. A sua cena gastronómica por si só atrai visitantes repetidos.

attractions.name: Terras Altas Cameron
attractions.desc: Um planalto fresco de montanha coberto de plantações de chá em socalcos, quintas de morango e pedaços de floresta musgosa, um contraste marcado com o calor tropical no resto do país. Caminhadas guiadas pela selva atravessam a Floresta Musgosa, com árvores atrofiadas e cobertas de líquenes. Excursões e provas em quintas de chá são o principal atrativo para a maioria dos visitantes.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional de Kinabalu, Bornéu
attractions.desc: Casa do Monte Kinabalu, o pico mais alto do Sudeste Asiático fora dos Himalaias, escalável em dois dias pela maioria dos caminhantes razoavelmente em forma com uma autorização e guia. O parque circundante também protege uma biodiversidade extraordinária, incluindo plantas carnívoras encontradas em mais lado nenhum. É normalmente combinado com uma viagem para ver orangotangos noutro local de Sabah.

attractions.name: Centro de Vida Selvagem de Semenggoh
attractions.desc: Um centro de reabilitação em Sarawak, Bornéu, onde orangotangos semi-selvagens outrora órfãos ou feridos regressam durante horários de alimentação programados. Os avistamentos não são garantidos já que os orangotangos procuram comida livremente na floresta circundante, o que acrescenta ao atrativo de os ver num ambiente genuinamente próximo do selvagem. É uma das formas mais acessíveis de ver orangotangos na Malásia.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–3
itinerary.title: Kuala Lumpur
itinerary.desc: As Torres Petronas, as Grutas de Batu, e a variada cena gastronómica da cidade.

itinerary.label: Dia 4
itinerary.title: Terras Altas Cameron
itinerary.desc: Plantações de chá e uma pausa de clima fresco face às terras baixas tropicais.

itinerary.label: Dias 5–6
itinerary.title: Penang
itinerary.desc: As ruas antigas de George Town, arte de rua e comida hawker.
itinerary.logistics: ~3h de carro desde as Terras Altas Cameron

itinerary.label: Dias 7–10
itinerary.title: Bornéu (Sabah/Sarawak)
itinerary.desc: Avistamentos de orangotangos e, para os mais ambiciosos, uma subida ao Monte Kinabalu.

goodToKnow.tipping: Não é obrigatório; a taxa de serviço já está muitas vezes incluída
goodToKnow.safety: Muito seguro; precauções normais em zonas movimentadas da cidade
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Voos domésticos são a forma mais fácil de chegar a Bornéu a partir da península
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KUL) is the main gateway for this route

food.name: Nasi lemak
food.desc: Arroz de coco servido com sambal, anchovas fritas, amendoins e ovo — considerado o prato nacional.

food.name: Char kway teow
food.desc: Noodles de arroz achatados salteados com camarão, ovo e rebentos de feijão, uma especialidade de Penang.

food.name: Laksa
food.desc: Uma sopa de noodles picante com variações regionais, desde à base de caril até caldos ácidos de tamarindo.

food.name: Roti canai
food.desc: Um pão achatado e estaladiço servido com molho de caril para molhar, popular a qualquer hora do dia.
